sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars, and I'm here today with a friend of the show and frequent 99PI contributor, Katie Thornton.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯，今天和我在一起的是本节目的老朋友、99PI的常客凯蒂·桑顿。

sentences.en: Hey, Katie, what do you have for us today?
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯蒂，今天给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So a while back, I was on this show talking about shortwave radio.
sentences.zh: 是这样，前阵子我在这档节目里聊过短波广播。

sentences.en: Unlike FM or AM radio, shortwave signals are those ones that can travel thousands of miles.
sentences.zh: 与调频或调幅广播不同，短波信号可以传播数千英里。

sentences.en: Yeah, you could be sitting in your place in Minnesota and like hear a broadcast in Spanish from South America or something with shortwave.
sentences.zh: 没错，你坐在明尼苏达州的家里，用短波就能听到来自南美洲的西班牙语广播之类的节目。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's actually the language part that I wanted to talk with you about today.
sentences.zh: 其实，我今天想和你聊的正是关于语言的部分。

sentences.en: Because one day as I was researching and poking around on the shortwaves, I learned something that really surprised me.
sentences.zh: 因为有一天我在研究和探索短波时，学到了一些让我非常惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: Roman, did you know that the Chinese national government and until recently the Vatican aired programs on shortwave radio in, drumroll please, Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你知道吗？中国政府，还有直到最近才停止的梵蒂冈，都曾用世界语在短波电台上播放节目——请敲鼓助兴。

sentences.en: Esperanto, the invented language of Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 世界语，那种人造的世界语。

sentences.en: I'm a big fan.
sentences.zh: 我是它的忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没错。

sentences.en: So in fact, the Vatican to this day still does a thrice weekly podcast in Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 事实上，梵蒂冈至今仍每周三次用世界语制作播客。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So for the dedicated 99PI fans, we did an episode on Esperanto way back.
sentences.zh: 对于99PI的铁杆粉丝来说，我们很久以前做过一期关于世界语的节目。

sentences.en: I think it was 2010.
sentences.zh: 我想那是2010年。

sentences.en: I think it was like the first year of the show.
sentences.zh: 我觉得应该是节目开播的第一年。

sentences.en: But for people who didn't hear that story or simply don't know or remember, because I don't remember what's in that story.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些没听过那个故事，或者根本不知道、不记得的人来说——因为我也不记得那期节目里讲了什么——

sentences.en: What should we say here about Esperanto?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里该怎么介绍世界语呢？

sentences.en: So Esperanto is what linguists call a constructed language.
sentences.zh: 世界语是语言学家所说的“人造语言”。

sentences.en: The language isn't attached to a nation or a region and it didn't evolve from some other language over time.
sentences.zh: 这种语言不依附于任何国家或地区，也不是随着时间推移从其他语言演变而来的。

sentences.en: Instead, nearly 150 years ago, someone decided to sit down, probably at a desk with a pen and paper and just make it whole cloth.
sentences.zh: 相反，大约150年前，有人决定坐下来——可能是在书桌前，拿着纸笔——凭空创造了它。

sentences.en: Or as we say on the show, they designed it.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我们在节目中所说，他们“设计”了它。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: They designed it.
sentences.zh: 他们设计了它。

sentences.en: And from the very beginning, the goal behind this designed language was to make it incredibly easy to learn.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这种设计语言背后的目标就是让它变得极其易学。

sentences.en: That way, everyone in the world would just voluntarily take it up.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，全世界的人都会自愿学习它。

sentences.en: And once that happened, we'd all be able to understand one another.
sentences.zh: 一旦实现了这一点，我们所有人就都能互相理解了。

sentences.en: And of course, from there, the idea went, world peace would follow.
sentences.zh: 当然，按照这个思路，世界和平也就随之而来了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Big goals.
sentences.zh: 宏大的目标。

sentences.en: Big goals.
sentences.zh: 宏大的目标。

sentences.en: Kind of the biggest goal.
sentences.zh: 可以说是最宏大的目标了。

sentences.en: So, you know, when I first came across this Vatican Esperanto thing, it really sent me down this crazy months, I guess even years-long rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当我第一次接触到梵蒂冈世界语这件事时，它真的让我陷入了一个疯狂的、持续了几个月甚至几年的“兔子洞”。

sentences.en: So much so that I actually took to Duolingo to learn Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 以至于我真的开始用多邻国（Duolingo）学习世界语了。

sentences.en: Uh, post me labores in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 呃，post me labores in the paSt（我过去工作过）。

sentences.en: Me domes.
sentences.zh: Me domes（我睡觉）。

sentences.en: After I worked, I slept.
sentences.zh: 工作之后，我睡觉了。

sentences.en: Same, bro.
sentences.zh: 我也是，兄弟。

sentences.en: Cha-ching.
sentences.zh: 叮当。

sentences.en: Well, since you're, you know, at least Duolingo versed in Esperanto, I should say, saluton, Katie.
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然你至少在多邻国上对世界语有所涉猎，那我就该说：Saluton（你好），凯蒂。

sentences.en: Mia nomo estas Roman.
sentences.zh: Mia nomo estas Roman（我的名字是罗曼）。

sentences.en: Oh, vi comprenas Esperanto.
sentences.zh: Oh, vi comprenas Esperanto（哦，你懂世界语）。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, a little.
sentences.zh: 你知道，懂一点点。

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 一点点。

sentences.en: I mean, I mean, that's just like, hi, Katie, my name is Roman.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那只是在说“你好，凯蒂，我的名字是罗曼”。

sentences.en: And then you replied, oh, you understand Esperanto, which I don't actually, but I did dabble in Esperanto a little bit when I was younger.
sentences.zh: 然后你回答说“哦，你懂世界语”，其实我并不懂，但我年轻时确实稍微接触过一点世界语。

sentences.en: I was taught it in second grade.
sentences.zh: 我在二年级时学过它。

sentences.en: Probably the last elementary school program in the United States to ever teach Esperanto, as far as I can tell.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这可能是美国最后一所教授世界语的小学课程。

sentences.en: But I was really, that experience really stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 但那次经历真的让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, unlike you, I was never an Esperantist, but I remember hearing about the language as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 所以，和你不同，我从来不是世界语者，但我记得十几岁时听说过这种语言。

sentences.en: And at the time, I was definitely interested in the idea of a language that was rooted in this idea of mutual understanding and belonging, even if it was a bit overly earneSt.
sentences.zh: 当时，我确实对这种植根于相互理解和归属感的语言理念很感兴趣，尽管它显得有点过于真诚了。

sentences.en: But, you know, I was also in high school and working and doing life, so I sort of forgot about it, honestly.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，那时候我还在上高中，忙着工作和生活，所以老实说，我把它给忘了。

sentences.en: Yeah, life happens and you put Esperanto on the back burner.
sentences.zh: 没错，生活总会发生，你就会把世界语搁置一旁。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Sad, but true.
sentences.zh: 悲伤但真实。

sentences.en: But then this past summer, I revisited Esperanto for a story I reported in Harper's Magazine.
sentences.zh: 但去年夏天，为了给《哈珀杂志》写一篇报道，我又重新研究了世界语。

sentences.en: Because I was curious, like, in a world that is as divided as ours, I wanted to know why this group still believes in the power of this language to bring about peace.
sentences.zh: 因为我很好奇，在一个像我们这样分裂的世界里，我想知道为什么这个群体仍然相信这种语言能带来和平的力量。

sentences.en: And if they do indeed believe that, where does that optimism come from?
sentences.zh: 如果他们确实相信，那么这种乐观精神从何而来？

sentences.en: And look, this isn't a story where I come out the other side convinced that Esperanto is going to solve all of our probleMs.
sentences.zh: 听着，这并不是一个让我最终确信世界语能解决我们所有问题的报道。

sentences.en: But I do think there's something we can all learn from the people who are keeping this old, invented language alive.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，我们都能从那些让这种古老的人造语言保持活力的人身上学到一些东西。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's start from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们从头说起。

sentences.en: Where did Esperanto originally come from?
sentences.zh: 世界语最初是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I'll kick things off.
sentences.zh: 那么，我来开个头。

sentences.en: In the late 1800s in a town called Bialystok.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末，在一个叫比亚韦斯托克的小镇。

sentences.en: This was a town that was home to people of a variety of different ethnicities and religions and languages spoken in the home.
sentences.zh: 这个镇上住着各种不同民族、宗教和家庭语言的人。

sentences.en: This is Bridget O'Keefe, a historian of the Soviet Union and professor at Brooklyn College.
sentences.zh: 这位是布里奇特·奥基夫，苏联历史学家，布鲁克林学院教授。

sentences.en: She wrote a book about Esperanto and internationalism.
sentences.zh: 她写过一本关于世界语和国际主义的书。

sentences.en: You had Poles, you had Jews, you had Russians, you had Germans.
sentences.zh: 那里有波兰人、犹太人、俄罗斯人、德国人。

sentences.en: This was, Bialystok was part of a very multi-ethnic, right, borderland region of the Tsarist Empire.
sentences.zh: 比亚韦斯托克是沙皇俄国一个非常多民族的边境地区，对吧？

sentences.en: If you were to look at a map today, Bialystok is a city on the eastern border of Poland.
sentences.zh: 如果你看今天的地图，比亚韦斯托克是波兰东部边境的一座城市。

sentences.en: But in the 19th century, it was part of something called the Pale of Settlement,
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪，它是“定居区”的一部分，

sentences.en: which was the area of the Russian Empire where Jews were allowed to live permanently.
sentences.zh: 也就是俄罗斯帝国允许犹太人永久居住的区域。

sentences.en: Which they really couldn't do in the rest of the Russian Empire.
sentences.zh: 而在俄罗斯帝国的其他地方，他们实际上是无法做到这一点的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so this is where, in 1859, a kid named L.L.
sentences.zh: 就在这里，1859年，一个叫L.L.的孩子出生了。

sentences.en: Zamenhof is born.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫出生了。

sentences.en: Growing up in Bialystok, Zamenhof spoke Yiddish, Russian, and Polish.
sentences.zh: 在比亚韦斯托克长大，柴门霍夫会说意第绪语、俄语和波兰语。

sentences.en: And later he learned French, Latin, Greek, Hebrew, and English.
sentences.zh: 后来他又学会了法语、拉丁语、希腊语、希伯来语和英语。

sentences.en: Show off.
sentences.zh: 炫耀啊。

sentences.en: I know, such a flex.
sentences.zh: 我知道，太凡尔赛了。

sentences.en: He didn't even have Duolingo.
sentences.zh: 他当时甚至还没有多邻国。

sentences.en: How did he do it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: But in learning all these languages, he was also keenly aware of the tension that came with all these differences.
sentences.zh: 但在学习所有这些语言的过程中，他也敏锐地意识到了这些差异所带来的紧张关系。

sentences.en: What he remembered most of all were insults and bickering and acrimony and just like an undercurrent in the marketplace,
sentences.zh: 他记忆最深的是侮辱、争吵、尖刻，以及在市场上、

sentences.en: in the town square, of animosity, mistruSt.
sentences.zh: 在城镇广场上那种暗流涌动的敌意和不信任。

sentences.en: So from a pretty young age, Zamenhof had this idea to bring the world together under one language.
sentences.zh: 所以从很小的时候起，柴门霍夫就有了用一种语言将世界团结起来的想法。

sentences.en: Here's Bridget paraphrasing a piece of a letter that Zamenhof wrote.
sentences.zh: 这是布里奇特转述柴门霍夫写的一封信的内容。

sentences.en: In my soul, right, in my own little aching child's heart, I thought to myself, so much of this tension, so much of this animosity,
sentences.zh: 在我的灵魂深处，在我那颗幼小而痛苦的心里，我对自己说，如果只有一种共同的模式、一种共同的语体、一种共同的语言来交流，

sentences.en: so much of this mistrust would be obviated if only we had, right, like a common mode, a common register, a common language through which to talk.
sentences.zh: 那么这种紧张、这种敌意、这种不信任，就会消除大半。

sentences.en: And so as a kid, Zamenhof started constructing a language that he reasoned would be easy for anyone to learn.
sentences.zh: 于是，柴门霍夫从小就开始构建一种他认为任何人都能轻松学会的语言。

sentences.en: And if it was also fun to learn, he figured, people would opt into it as a second language.
sentences.zh: 他想，如果学起来也很有趣，人们就会选择把它作为第二语言。

sentences.en: And voila, marketplace arguments over.
sentences.zh: 瞧，市场上的争吵结束了。

sentences.en: I'm sort of struck by the sort of the childlike approach to Zamenhof's project.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫项目的这种孩子气的方法让我很受触动。

sentences.en: Like, you know, kids sometimes will create a secret code so they can talk to one another so that nobody understands them.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，孩子们有时会创造一种秘密代码来互相交流，这样别人就听不懂了。

sentences.en: But this is like the total opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 但这完全是反其道而行之。

sentences.en: Complete opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 完全相反。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wanted everybody to speak it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他希望每个人都说这种语言。

sentences.en: So starting when he was pretty young, Zamenhof crafted the rules of his language.
sentences.zh: 所以从很小的时候开始，柴门霍夫就制定了他这种语言的规则。

sentences.en: And in 1887, before his 30th birthday, he compiled all those rules and published what's called the first book or Unua Libro.
sentences.zh: 1887年，在他30岁生日前，他整理了所有规则，出版了所谓的“第一本书”或《Unua Libro》。

sentences.en: And this is the founding text, like the Bible, so to speak, for Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 这就是世界语的奠基之作，可以说是世界语的《圣经》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this book was actually written in Russian.
sentences.zh: 这本书实际上是用俄语写的。

sentences.en: So technically, the book's title is just international language.
sentences.zh: 所以从技术上讲，书名只是“国际语言”。

sentences.en: And Zamenhof actually wrote it under the pen name Doctoro Esperanto, which in his own language means one who hopes.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫实际上是用笔名“世界语博士”（Doctoro Esperanto）写的，在他的语言里，这意味着“心怀希望的人”。

sentences.en: So Esperanto comes from that pen name, Doctoro Esperanto?
sentences.zh: 所以世界语（Esperanto）这个名字来自那个笔名“世界语博士”？

sentences.en: Yeah, he did not actually name this thing Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 是的，他实际上并没有把这种语言命名为世界语。

sentences.en: That was all the work of the fans.
sentences.zh: 那全是粉丝们的功劳。

sentences.en: They took the name like Dr. Frankenstein and Frankenstein.
sentences.zh: 他们就像对待弗兰肯斯坦博士和弗兰肯斯坦怪物那样取了名字。

sentences.en: Yes, it's exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's exactly like that.
sentences.zh: 完全就是那样。

sentences.en: And in this book, Zamenhof, or Doctoro Esperanto, lays out the language's ideology of unity and peace.
sentences.zh: 在这本书里，柴门霍夫，或者说“世界语博士”，阐述了这种语言关于团结与和平的意识形态。

sentences.en: But mostly what he does is outline the grammar, the word structure, really the design of the language.
sentences.zh: 但他主要做的是概述语法、词汇结构，也就是这种语言的设计。

sentences.en: The way that Zamenhof designed the language was to give birth to a kind of core vocabulary of, you know, some 700, 900 core root words.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫设计这种语言的方式是创造出一种核心词汇，大约有700到900个核心词根。

sentences.en: So what Zamenhof does is make it so that all of the parts of speech, nouns, adjectives, adverbs, verbs, have a consistent ending.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫的做法是让所有的词性——名词、形容词、副词、动词——都有统一的词尾。

sentences.en: This is the best part of Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 这是世界语最棒的地方。

sentences.en: So please explain this a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 请再多解释一下这个。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 好的，当然。

sentences.en: It's so good.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Nouns end in O, so sano is health.
sentences.zh: 名词以O结尾，所以sano是健康。

sentences.en: Adjectives end in A, sana is healthy.
sentences.zh: 形容词以A结尾，sana是健康的。

sentences.en: Verbs end in I, so sani, to be healthy.
sentences.zh: 动词以I结尾，所以sani是保持健康。

sentences.en: And there are also the prefixes and suffixes that modify, like mal indicates the opposite.
sentences.zh: 还有一些修饰词的前缀和后缀，比如mal表示相反。

sentences.en: And so, like, sana is healthy, but malsana is sick.
sentences.zh: 所以，sana是健康的，而malsana就是生病的。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay, look at you, Roman, reaching back to your Esperanto roots and prefixes and affixes.
sentences.zh: 没错，好吧，罗曼，看看你，又回想起你的世界语词根、前缀和后缀了。

sentences.en: But yes, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 但没错，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's really clear, really simple, and consistent.
sentences.zh: 它非常清晰、简单且一致。

sentences.en: Esperanto advocates like to say that you can understand the vast majority of the language just from knowing about 500 plug-and-play root words and affixes.
sentences.zh: 世界语倡导者喜欢说，只要掌握大约500个即插即用的词根和词缀，就能理解绝大多数语言内容。

sentences.en: And so, while he kind of gave the language its original architecture and gave it its original vocabulary,
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然他为这种语言提供了最初的架构和词汇，

sentences.en: so much of even the earliest vocabulary was just developed in the practice of, at first,
sentences.zh: 但即使是最早的词汇，也有很大一部分是在实践中发展出来的，起初是

sentences.en: a dozen and then dozens and then hundreds and then thousands and then tens of thousands of people actually putting the language into practice.
sentences.zh: 十几个人，然后几十人、几百人、几千人，最后是成千上万的人真正地将这种语言付诸实践。

sentences.en: So, I should say, Zamenhof wasn't the first to think of creating a universal second language.
sentences.zh: 所以，我应该说，柴门霍夫并不是第一个想到创造通用第二语言的人。

sentences.en: In the late 1800s, attempts at creating something like Esperanto were actually pretty common.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末，尝试创造类似世界语的东西其实很常见。

sentences.en: New technologies like railroads were connecting people across huge distances,
sentences.zh: 铁路等新技术将相隔遥远的人们连接在一起，

sentences.en: and there was this notion that maybe language would be the next great divide to fall.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种观念认为，语言可能是下一个即将消失的巨大鸿沟。

sentences.en: But unlike those other attempts, Esperanto actually caught on.
sentences.zh: 但与其他尝试不同，世界语确实流行起来了。

sentences.en: But I'm curious, like, how does that happen?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: Like, how does word get out about Esperanto?
sentences.zh: 关于世界语的消息是怎么传开的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the language isn't just growing because it's easy to learn.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种语言的增长不仅仅是因为它易学。

sentences.en: Of course, that helps.
sentences.zh: 当然，那也有帮助。

sentences.en: But on top of everything, Zamenhof is also kind of a marketing mastermind.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，柴门霍夫还是一位营销天才。

sentences.en: So, in the back of the Unua Libro, there were these little pre-printed notes that you could tear out of the book saying that you promised to learn Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 在《第一书》的末尾，印有一些可以撕下来的预印便条，上面写着你承诺学习世界语。

sentences.en: So, and people would essentially make these pledges, these promises, and then mail the note back to Zamenhof personally.
sentences.zh: 人们基本上会做出这些保证和承诺，然后亲自把便条寄回给柴门霍夫。

sentences.en: Whenever an Esperantist or a young early adopter or even someone just curious wrote to him, he would reply.
sentences.zh: 每当有世界语者、年轻的早期采用者，甚至是单纯好奇的人写信给他，他都会回复。

sentences.en: But what he would also do is he started creating an address book, a directory of people who signed their names,
sentences.zh: 但他还会做一件事，他开始建立一个通讯录，收录那些签了名的人，

sentences.en: who had committed to learning the language, and who had expressed interest in corresponding or communicating in it.
sentences.zh: 那些承诺学习这门语言，并表示有兴趣用它进行通信或交流的人。

sentences.en: This is so amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了。

sentences.en: Like, so people are sending their pledges into Zamenhof, and then he's compiling basically like a directory of speakers.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，人们把他们的承诺寄给柴门霍夫，然后他基本上是在汇编一份演讲者名录。

sentences.en: And then does he publish this directory?
sentences.zh: 那他会出版这份名录吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, you could go get your own copy of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以去买一份属于你自己的副本。

sentences.en: And people would write letters to other Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 人们会给其他世界语者写信。

sentences.en: It was a really big grassroots movement.
sentences.zh: 这真是一场声势浩大的草根运动。

sentences.en: The Unua Libro, with the grammar and everything, had to be reprinted within six months of its debut.
sentences.zh: 《第一书》及其语法等内容，在首次出版后的六个月内就不得不重印了。

sentences.en: And by the turn of the century, the movement had gained enough momentum to really begin to organize.
sentences.zh: 到了世纪之交，这场运动已经积聚了足够的动力，开始真正组织起来。

sentences.en: In 1905, for the first time in world history,
sentences.zh: 1905年，在世界历史上第一次，

sentences.en: a group of electing Esperantists travel to France as participants in the first World Congress of Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 一群世界语者前往法国，参加了第一届世界世界语大会。

sentences.en: This first World Congress of Esperantists is really just a fancy way of saying that they held a convention.
sentences.zh: 这第一届世界世界语大会，其实就是他们举办了一次集会的华丽说法。

sentences.en: And at this first convention, nearly 700 people joined from more than 20 countries.
sentences.zh: 在这次首届大会上，来自20多个国家的近700人参加了会议。

sentences.en: They found that Esperanto could actually work in real life, right?
sentences.zh: 他们发现世界语在现实生活中确实行得通，对吧？

sentences.en: It could work in live conversation, that it had a life beyond the page, right?
sentences.zh: 它可以在现场对话中发挥作用，它在书本之外还有生命，对吧？

sentences.en: It allowed them to meet people and to talk to people and to have fun with people and to realize, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 它让他们能够结识他人、与人交谈、与人共度欢乐时光，并意识到，你知道，比如，

sentences.en: oh, I've been spending hours with these people, and I'm not thinking about them as Frenchmen or as Englishmen or as Russians or as Jews.
sentences.zh: 哦，我和这些人在一起待了几个小时，我并没有把他们看作法国人、英国人、俄罗斯人或犹太人。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about them as people.
sentences.zh: 我把他们看作是人。

sentences.en: So this is clearly a big deal, and that's a lot of people to get together from so many different places in 1905.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然是一件大事，在1905年能让来自这么多不同地方的人聚在一起，人数可不少。

sentences.en: But, like, beyond the convention, is it well known?
sentences.zh: 但是，除了大会之外，它广为人知吗？

sentences.en: Like, is Esperanto really in the zeitgeist?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，世界语真的在时代精神中吗？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: You know, it was an explicitly internationals project, so it particularly took off among leftist groups,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个明确的国际主义项目，所以它在左翼团体中特别受欢迎，

sentences.en: like international labor organizers and anarchists.
sentences.zh: 比如国际劳工组织者和无政府主义者。

sentences.en: It also had some big-name boosters.
sentences.zh: 它还有一些大人物的支持。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe you've heard of a guy with just a little bit of influence, this Christian anarchist pacifist, Leo Tolstoy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可能听说过一个有点影响力的人，这位基督教无政府主义和平主义者，列夫·托尔斯泰。

sentences.en: So Tolstoy took it upon himself to learn Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 所以托尔斯泰亲自学习了世界语。

sentences.en: Ho Chi Minh learned it while living in London.
sentences.zh: 胡志明在伦敦生活时也学习了它。

sentences.en: And actually, George Soros' father, who was born Tibidar Schwartz,
sentences.zh: 事实上，乔治·索罗斯的父亲，原名蒂比达尔·施瓦茨，

sentences.en: he changed his family's last name to the Esperanto word meaning Will Soar.
sentences.zh: 他把家人的姓氏改成了世界语中意为“将要翱翔”的词。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And that was to avoid anti-Semitic persecution in his native Hungary.
sentences.zh: 那是为了避免在他祖国匈牙利遭受反犹太主义的迫害。

sentences.en: I did not know that at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道这一点。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: A lot of prominent speakers, a ton of speakers.
sentences.zh: 很多杰出的演讲者，大量的演讲者。

sentences.en: I mean, this was really a thing at the time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这在当时确实是一件大事。

sentences.en: But what I'm wondering is, like, all this popularity and growth is happening,
sentences.zh: 但我好奇的是，这种流行和增长正在发生，

sentences.en: it actually presents this challenge for a designed language like Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 它实际上给世界语这种设计语言带来了挑战。

sentences.en: Because as soon as more people start speaking it,
sentences.zh: 因为一旦更多的人开始说它，

sentences.en: don't they start changing the language with their own verb tenses and their own slang?
sentences.zh: 他们难道不会用自己的动词时态和俚语来改变这门语言吗？

sentences.en: Like, doesn't it stop from being this, like, fixed, universal, second language
sentences.zh: 比如，它难道不会停止成为这种固定的、通用的第二语言，

sentences.en: into something that evolves naturally, like, natural languages do?
sentences.zh: 而变成像自然语言那样自然演变的东西吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so that does begin to happen.
sentences.zh: 是的，这种情况确实开始发生了。

sentences.en: And it's a really big concern for the early Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 这对早期的世界语者来说是一个非常大的担忧。

sentences.en: So at that first annual convention in France,
sentences.zh: 所以在法国举行的第一届年度大会上，

sentences.en: some Esperantists at Samenhoff's urging formed what came to be called the Esperanto Academy,
sentences.zh: 一些世界语者在柴门霍夫的敦促下成立了后来被称为世界语学院的机构，

sentences.en: which is basically like a governing body for the language to keep Esperanto from changing uncontrollably.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就像是这门语言的管理机构，以防止世界语发生无法控制的变化。

sentences.en: And this is actually pretty common.
sentences.zh: 这其实很常见。

sentences.en: Like, lots of languages, they have their own institutions that regulate linguistic standards.
sentences.zh: 比如，许多语言都有自己的机构来规范语言标准。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: There's one in Spain for Spanish.
sentences.zh: 西班牙就有一个针对西班牙语的机构。

sentences.en: But the goal is a little bit different because with, you know, Spanish and French academies,
sentences.zh: 但目标有点不同，因为你知道，西班牙语和法语学院，

sentences.en: the goal is to define a sort of national identity around the language.
sentences.zh: 目标是围绕语言定义一种民族认同。

sentences.en: But in Esperanto, the goal is to keep it, you know, simple, straightforward, consistent,
sentences.zh: 但在世界语中，目标是保持它的简单、直接、一致，

sentences.en: so that it as a language can transcend all national boundaries.
sentences.zh: 这样它作为一种语言就能超越所有的国家界限。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And it did do that.
sentences.zh: 它确实做到了。

sentences.en: Esperanto is rooted in European languages, but it didn't just take off in Europe.
sentences.zh: 世界语植根于欧洲语言，但它不仅仅在欧洲流行。

sentences.en: It found an early foothold in Asia and eventually around the globe.
sentences.zh: 它在亚洲找到了早期的立足点，并最终遍布全球。

sentences.en: And for a lot of early speakers, this was all part of the plan.
sentences.zh: 对于许多早期的使用者来说，这都是计划的一部分。

sentences.en: So what do you mean by here, by the plan?
sentences.zh: 那你说的“计划”是指什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so we mentioned that the idea behind this language was that everybody would speak it,
sentences.zh: 好的，我们提到过这门语言背后的想法是每个人都会说它，

sentences.en: understand one another, inevitably there would be peace.
sentences.zh: 彼此理解，不可避免地就会有和平。

sentences.en: For a lot of the early Esperantists, that wasn't just a sort of passing idea.
sentences.zh: 对于许多早期的世界语者来说，那不仅仅是一个转瞬即逝的想法。

sentences.en: It was a real political project.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的政治项目。

sentences.en: From the early days of the language, people in the Esperanto movement had this concept called the Fina Venko, final victory.
sentences.zh: 从这门语言的早期开始，世界语运动中的人们就有了这个概念，叫做“最终胜利”。

sentences.en: That would occur when everyone in the world, including governments, would take up Esperanto as a second language,
sentences.zh: 当世界上每个人，包括政府，都采用世界语作为第二语言时，就会实现这一点，

sentences.en: and the people would be united in a shared tongue.
sentences.zh: 人们将通过共同的语言团结起来。

sentences.en: It's an ideology that came to be known as Fina Venkismo.
sentences.zh: 这是一种后来被称为“最终胜利主义”的意识形态。

sentences.en: That's pretty intense.
sentences.zh: 这太强烈了。

sentences.en: I don't like any political movements that are the final anything, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不喜欢任何以“最终”结尾的政治运动。

sentences.en: Yeah, me neither.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也不喜欢。

sentences.en: But, you know, in the early 1900s, Fina Venkismo felt possible.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在20世纪初，“最终胜利主义”感觉是可能的。

sentences.en: The language was reaching all kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 这门语言正在触及各种各样的人。

sentences.en: But, you know, we're not all speaking Esperanto today.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们今天并不是都在说世界语。

sentences.en: So, of course, at some point, this all must start to flicker out.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，在某个时候，这一切肯定开始逐渐消退。

sentences.en: Yeah, big time.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常严重。

sentences.en: Precisely in that decade where Esperanto was truly taking off, right, like it was truly like having its moment, right,
sentences.zh: 恰恰是在世界语真正腾飞的那十年里，对吧，就像它真正拥有了属于自己的时刻，对吧，

sentences.en: there were kind of factions that argued, right, that Esperanto was great, but it could be better.
sentences.zh: 有一些派别争论说，世界语很棒，但可以更好。

sentences.en: We could, like, fine-tune this and perfect this more.
sentences.zh: 我们可以微调并完善它。

sentences.en: So, in 1907 comes the first major, what I'll call, I-have-a-better-idea moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，1907年出现了第一个重大的，我称之为“我有一个更好的主意”的时刻。

sentences.en: And it comes in the form of a new language called Edo.
sentences.zh: 它以一种名为“伊多语”的新语言形式出现。

sentences.en: The Edo speakers, or the E-dists, were originally Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 伊多语的使用者，或称伊多主义者，最初都是世界语者。

sentences.en: In fact, the name Edo actually comes from the Esperanto affix meaning offspring.
sentences.zh: 事实上，“伊多”这个名字实际上来自世界语中意为“后代”的词缀。

sentences.en: And the E-dists created what was essentially Esperanto with even more straightforward grammar
sentences.zh: 伊多主义者创造了一种本质上是语法更直接、

sentences.en: and even more simplified vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 词汇更简化的世界语。

sentences.en: And all this tinkering with the language really started to divide the Esperanto movement.
sentences.zh: 所有这些对语言的修补确实开始分裂世界语运动。

sentences.en: When you're really passionate about something, you can miss the forest for the trees and you can forget your audience.
sentences.zh: 当你对某件事充满热情时，你可能会只见树木不见森林，忘记你的受众。

sentences.en: And it was, like, one of the things that was illustrative of how the Esperanto movement got in its own way.
sentences.zh: 这正是说明世界语运动如何阻碍自身发展的事情之一。

sentences.en: So, this missing the forest for the trees thing, it just keeps happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种“只见树木不见森林”的事情，一直在发生。

sentences.en: Because as the language grew and by design welcomed all sorts of people,
sentences.zh: 因为随着语言的发展，并且按照设计欢迎各种各样的人，

sentences.en: the foundational aspirations of Esperanto kept being tested.
sentences.zh: 世界语的基本愿望不断受到考验。

sentences.en: The movement itself had an extraordinary tendency to create its own splinters.
sentences.zh: 运动本身有一种非凡的倾向，即制造自己的分裂。

sentences.en: We have bourgeois Esperantists over here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有资产阶级世界语者。

sentences.en: We have socialist Esperantists over here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有社会主义世界语者。

sentences.en: We have anarchist Esperantists over here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有无政府主义世界语者。

sentences.en: There's something ironic about the fact that there are these bitter rifts that are breaking out inside of this language
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，在这门本应将我们所有人团结在一起的语言内部，却爆发了这些激烈的裂痕。

sentences.en: that's supposed to be bringing us all together.
sentences.zh: 这确实很讽刺。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And of course, like, that is not exclusive to Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是世界语所独有的。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: It happens in all sorts of movements.
sentences.zh: 它发生在各种各样的运动中。

sentences.en: People genuinely want to come together.
sentences.zh: 人们真心希望团结在一起。

sentences.en: They are desperate to come together.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望团结在一起。

sentences.en: But sometimes one of the biggest barriers to actually living in harmony
sentences.zh: 但有时实现和谐生活最大的障碍之一，

sentences.en: is a disagreement over the best way to live in harmony.
sentences.zh: 是对实现和谐的最佳方式存在分歧。

sentences.en: It's deeply frustrating, but also deeply human.
sentences.zh: 这令人深感沮丧，但也非常人性化。

sentences.en: Yeah, and also kind of beautiful in its own right.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且它本身也有一种美感。

sentences.en: And so all along, there are certainly internal forces that are fracturing the Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 所以一直以来，确实有内部力量在分裂世界语者。

sentences.en: But soon, external forces begin to really reshape the movement as well.
sentences.zh: 但很快，外部力量也开始真正重塑这场运动。

sentences.en: So in the 1920s and 30s, nationalists were growing in power around the world,
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪20年代和30年代，民族主义者在世界各地势力壮大，

sentences.en: and they swiftly moved to end all internationalist agendas.
sentences.zh: 他们迅速采取行动，终结了所有的国际主义议程。

sentences.en: So Franco, Stalin, and Hitler's regimes all criminalized Esperanto,
sentences.zh: 所以佛朗哥、斯大林和希特勒的政权都将世界语定为非法，

sentences.en: and sometimes executed Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 有时还会处决世界语者。

sentences.en: The Nazis even murdered all three of Zamenhof's children.
sentences.zh: 纳粹甚至杀害了柴门霍夫的全部三个孩子。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And yet, still, like, somehow the language survived.
sentences.zh: 然而，不知何故，这门语言还是幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, like, it was certainly seen as a threat.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实被视为一种威胁。

sentences.en: It was actively repressed.
sentences.zh: 它受到了积极的压制。

sentences.en: And it would never again be as popular as it was before the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 它再也不会像第二次世界大战前那样受欢迎了。

sentences.en: But when the most violent repression eased after the war,
sentences.zh: 但当战后最暴力的压制缓解后，

sentences.en: Esperanto, once again, had a bit of a boom.
sentences.zh: 世界语再次迎来了一波繁荣。

sentences.en: This time during the Cold War, both among young people in the Soviet Union
sentences.zh: 这一次是在冷战期间，既在苏联的年轻人中，

sentences.en: who wanted to connect with people in Western Europe,
sentences.zh: 他们想与西欧的人们建立联系，

sentences.en: but also among folks in Eastern Europe who were trying to resist the sort of snowballing hegemony of the West
sentences.zh: 也包括东欧那些试图抵制西方和英语日益增长的霸权的人们。

sentences.en: and of the English language.
sentences.zh: 而且我从个人经验中知道，它在70年代和80年代的嬉皮士知识分子运动、后嬉皮士运动中再次绽放。

sentences.en: And I know from personal experience that it kind of bloomed again in the sort of, like,
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: you know, hippie intellectual movement, the post-hippie movement in the 70s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 然后到了90年代，有一个庞大的使用者社区将这门语言带到了网上，

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 让越来越多的人更容易在网上学习。

sentences.en: And then in the 90s, there's a big community of speakers who brought the language online
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: and made it easier for more and more people to learn on the web.
sentences.zh: 看在上帝的份上，它甚至在多邻国上都有。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 叮当。

sentences.en: It's on Duolingo for Jizo's sake.
sentences.zh: 所以给你，柴门霍夫。

sentences.en: Cha-ching.
sentences.zh: 我们真的做到了。

sentences.en: So there you go, Zamanov.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想这真的让我们回到了起点。

sentences.en: We really did it.
sentences.zh: 比如，你去年学习了世界语。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I guess that really brings us back to where we started.
sentences.zh: 那么你最终为了这个故事和任何世界语者交谈了吗？

sentences.en: Like, you learned Esperanto last year.
sentences.zh: 是的，我谈了。

sentences.en: So did you end up speaking with any Esperantists for this story?
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，网上有一个繁荣的世界语者社区，Facebook群组，Reddit子版块。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想亲自见到人们，找出这些仍然在学习和说这种本应给世界带来和平的19世纪语言的人到底是谁。

sentences.en: So there's, of course, a thriving community of Esperantists online, Facebook groups, subreddits.
sentences.zh: 所以去年夏天，我飞越半个地球来到捷克共和国的一个小城市布尔诺，

sentences.en: But I really wanted to meet people, like, in person and find out who are these folks who are still learning
sentences.zh: 去寻找答案。

sentences.en: and speaking this 19th century language that was supposed to bring peace to the world.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: So last summer, I flew halfway around the world to Brno, a small city in the Czech Republic,
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个非常迷人的故事。

sentences.en: because for eight days, more than a thousand Esperantists from all over were gathered here for the World Esperanto Congress.
sentences.zh: 因为在过去的八天里，来自世界各地的一千多名世界语者聚集在这里，参加世界世界语大会。

sentences.en: Eight days?
sentences.zh: 八天？

sentences.en: Eight days.
sentences.zh: 八天。

sentences.en: Eight days.
sentences.zh: 八天。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: So that convention happens every year?
sentences.zh: 所以那个大会每年都举办吗？

sentences.en: Every year, Roman.
sentences.zh: 每年都办，罗曼。

sentences.en: And while it's happening, everyone basically only speaks Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 而且在大会期间，大家基本上只说世界语。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Also, I should say the Esperantists prefer to call it the Universale Congreso de Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 另外，我应该说世界语者更喜欢称它为“世界世界语大会”。

sentences.en: Okay, so after the break, Katie reports from the Universale Congreso de Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 好的，休息之后，凯蒂将从世界世界语大会现场发回报道。

sentences.en: So stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Okay, so we're back and we're at the convention.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们回来了，现在就在大会现场。

sentences.en: And I think someone said something like, hello and welcome to Brno.
sentences.zh: 我想刚才有人说了类似“你好，欢迎来到布尔诺”的话。

sentences.en: Hey, not bad for someone who only dabbled in Esperanto 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 嘿，对于一个40年前才浅尝辄止学过世界语的人来说，这还不错。

sentences.en: But yes, I'm there in Brno with more than a thousand Esperanto speakers from 62 different countries.
sentences.zh: 没错，我当时就在布尔诺，和来自62个不同国家的一千多名世界语使用者在一起。

sentences.en: And when I arrived at the convention, I was kind of shocked to see the breadth of people speaking Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 当我到达大会现场时，看到世界语使用者的广泛程度，我感到有些震惊。

sentences.en: There were, as ever, the anarchists and the European Social Democrats.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，那里有无政府主义者，也有欧洲社会民主党人。

sentences.en: But there were also folks from a state-approved Chinese Esperantist group, a delegation from the Catholic Church, Ukrainian independence advocates.
sentences.zh: 但也有来自官方认可的中国世界语者团体的成员、天主教会的代表，以及乌克兰独立倡导者。

sentences.en: So, like, really a range of people from all over with perhaps, like, a pretty wide range of political views.
sentences.zh: 所以，真的有一群来自各地、可能有着相当广泛政治观点的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that surprised me.
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我很惊讶。

sentences.en: I assumed I'd be running into a lot of left-leaning American nerdy types.
sentences.zh: 我本以为会遇到很多左倾的美国书呆子类型的人。

sentences.en: No offense, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，没有冒犯的意思。

sentences.en: But that wasn't really the case.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And I also presumed that the convention would be pretty in line with the traditional goals of Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 而且我还以为大会会非常符合世界语的传统目标。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of talk about the language, about how the movement can bring about peace.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多关于语言的讨论，关于这场运动如何带来和平的讨论。

sentences.en: And there was a bit of that.
sentences.zh: 确实有那么一点。

sentences.en: But what I didn't expect was that most people didn't really talk much about those ideals at all.
sentences.zh: 但我没想到的是，大多数人根本没怎么谈论那些理想。

sentences.en: So I want to get to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: But let's start with the old-school stuff and what was maybe the most traditional of all the sessions at the convention.
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从老派的东西开始，看看大会上最传统的一场会议。

sentences.en: The public meeting of the Academia de Esperanto, or the Esperanto Academy.
sentences.zh: 世界语学院的公开会议。

sentences.en: Oh, so the Esperanto Academy, it still exists.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以世界语学院还存在啊。

sentences.en: It does still exiSt.
sentences.zh: 它确实还存在。

sentences.en: And they still do largely the same job that they started back in 1905.
sentences.zh: 而且他们所做的工作在很大程度上与1905年刚开始时一样。

sentences.en: They hold public meetings and discuss how the language is evolving.
sentences.zh: 他们举行公开会议，讨论语言是如何演变的。

sentences.en: Now, before you get your hopes up for a raucous session full of debate about grammar and syntax,
sentences.zh: 现在，在你对一场充满语法和句法辩论的激烈会议抱有期待之前，

sentences.en: I want to explain that this was not the most thrilling session that I went to at the convention.
sentences.zh: 我想说明的是，这并不是我参加过的最激动人心的会议。

sentences.en: There was no shouting matches.
sentences.zh: 没有争吵。

sentences.en: There honestly weren't that many people there even.
sentences.zh: 老实说，甚至没多少人参加。

sentences.en: But, you know, sometimes this is what democracy looks like.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这就是民主有时看起来的样子。

sentences.en: Slow, a little boring, kind of poorly attended.
sentences.zh: 缓慢，有点无聊，出席率有点低。

sentences.en: And so what was happening in this session?
sentences.zh: 那么那场会议上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So basically, people were submitting questions on pieces of paper.
sentences.zh: 基本上，人们把问题写在纸条上提交上去。

sentences.en: At one point, you know, somebody submitted a question about why the language doesn't yet have a great and broadly accepted gender-neutral pronoun.
sentences.zh: 有一次，有人提问为什么这门语言还没有一个出色且被广泛接受的性别中立代词。

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: Totally valid question.
sentences.zh: 完全合理的问题。

sentences.en: So the Academy took that under advisement.
sentences.zh: 所以学院把这个问题纳入了考量。

sentences.en: There was also a question from a violin repair person asking why there weren't more words for stringed instruments in the latest official dictionary.
sentences.zh: 还有一个小提琴修理工提问，为什么最新的官方词典里没有更多关于弦乐器的词汇。

sentences.en: Fun.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: So the questions, they really ran the gamut.
sentences.zh: 所以这些问题，真的是五花八门。

sentences.en: So did you muster up some courage and ask a question of the Academy?
sentences.zh: 那你有没有鼓起勇气向学院提问？

sentences.en: I did not feel that I'm a competent enough Esperanto speaker to know of any missing words or confusing grammar.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己的世界语水平还不够高，不知道有什么缺失的词汇或令人困惑的语法。

sentences.en: But I did get to talk with an organizer who helped set up the Congress.
sentences.zh: 但我确实和一位协助筹办大会的组织者聊了聊。

sentences.en: His name is Petro Balas.
sentences.zh: 他叫彼得罗·巴拉斯。

sentences.en: And what I learned from talking with him and others is that the Academy is a pretty reactive group.
sentences.zh: 通过与他和其他人交谈，我了解到学院是一个相当被动的组织。

sentences.en: Like, they don't want to upset their fellow Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 他们不想惹恼其他世界语者。

sentences.en: So once a word or a way of speaking becomes commonplace within the community, the Academy kind of reviews it.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦某个词或某种表达方式在社区内变得普遍，学院就会进行审查。

sentences.en: And often they make a recommendation that others adopted, too.
sentences.zh: 他们通常会提出建议，其他人也会采纳。

sentences.en: Of course, they are only the recommendations because the community of Esperantists there more tend to be, like, anarchists.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些只是建议，因为那里的世界语者社区往往更倾向于无政府主义者。

sentences.en: Okay, so tell me more about Petro.
sentences.zh: 好的，多跟我说说彼得罗吧。

sentences.en: What's going on with Petro?
sentences.zh: 彼得罗那边怎么样？

sentences.en: Yeah, Petro was born in then Czechoslovakia, and he started learning and speaking Esperanto a few years after watching his country split in two.
sentences.zh: 嗯，彼得罗出生在当时的捷克斯洛伐克，他在目睹国家一分为二几年后开始学习和说世界语。

sentences.en: And he told me that Esperanto speakers these days come to the Congress not necessarily to talk about grammar and syntax.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，如今的世界语者来参加大会，并不一定是为了讨论语法和句法。

sentences.en: They come for the community and for the camaraderie.
sentences.zh: 他们是为了社区和友谊而来。

sentences.en: And did you see that play out at the Congress?
sentences.zh: 你在大会上看到这种情况了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I definitely did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实看到了。

sentences.en: Like, many of the most spirited and well-attended sessions at the convention weren't the super official things, like the Academy session that I went to.
sentences.zh: 大会上许多最活跃、出席人数最多的会议，并不是那些超级官方的活动，比如我参加的学院会议。

sentences.en: Instead, there was a lot of energy around the hobbies and the social gatherings.
sentences.zh: 相反，围绕爱好和社交聚会的活动非常有活力。

sentences.en: So you can meet here, like, linguists, professors.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这里见到语言学家、教授。

sentences.en: You can meet here, like, chess players or Go players and whatever.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这里见到国际象棋棋手或围棋棋手等等。

sentences.en: So over the course of the trip, I met, yes, Esperanto's chess players and Go players.
sentences.zh: 所以在整个旅程中，我确实遇到了世界语的国际象棋棋手和围棋棋手。

sentences.en: There were also bicycle enthusiasts and stamp collectors.
sentences.zh: 还有自行车爱好者和集邮爱好者。

sentences.en: Even Esperanto nudists had events.
sentences.zh: 甚至连世界语裸体主义者都有活动。

sentences.en: Like, they went to a nude beach and they all crammed on this public tram to get there for a half hour.
sentences.zh: 他们去了裸体海滩，为了去那里，他们挤了半小时的公共电车。

sentences.en: And, I mean, maybe the hottest ticket of the entire week, or at least a personal favorite of mine,
sentences.zh: 而且，我想，这可能是整个星期最热门的活动，或者至少是我个人的最爱，

sentences.en: was a presentation by the International Federation of Esperanto Railway Men.
sentences.zh: 是国际世界语铁路工作者联合会的演讲。

sentences.en: The train people.
sentences.zh: 铁路人。

sentences.en: I love the train people.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢铁路人。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The train people absolutely rocked.
sentences.zh: 铁路人的演讲简直太棒了。

sentences.en: Fantastic presentation.
sentences.zh: 精彩的演讲。

sentences.en: History of trains in Berno and beyond.
sentences.zh: 关于布尔诺及其他地方的火车历史。

sentences.en: I mean, this all sounds fun and funny, but it all makes total sense.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切听起来既有趣又好笑，但完全合情合理。

sentences.en: Like, you're an Esperanto speaker at an Esperanto convention.
sentences.zh: 你是一个在世界语大会上的世界语使用者。

sentences.en: You want to have fun.
sentences.zh: 你想玩得开心。

sentences.en: You want to speak the language.
sentences.zh: 你想说这门语言。

sentences.en: You don't want to just debate world peace or whatever goals, these high-minded goals that maybe get nowhere.
sentences.zh: 你不想只去辩论世界和平或其他什么目标，那些可能毫无进展的高尚目标。

sentences.en: You want to talk about trains.
sentences.zh: 你想谈论火车。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Of course you want to talk about trains.
sentences.zh: 你当然想谈论火车。

sentences.en: But, you know, the convention hasn't always been this sort of fun, social gathering.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，大会并不总是这种有趣的社交聚会。

sentences.en: That dynamic is actually the result of a pivotal moment for the movement.
sentences.zh: 这种动态实际上是该运动一个关键时刻的结果。

sentences.en: So, back in 1980, at an Esperanto Youth Congress in the Finnish city of Rauma, a group of speakers had an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 1980年，在芬兰城市劳马举行的世界语青年大会上，一群使用者有了顿悟。

sentences.en: They were like, hey, all these grand ambitions for world peace and universal second language,
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，嘿，所有这些关于世界和平和通用第二语言的宏大抱负，

sentences.en: they're really sort of weighing the movement down.
sentences.zh: 实际上是在拖累这场运动。

sentences.en: So, let's just close the book on all that.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们把这一切都翻篇吧。

sentences.en: So, they're basically kind of giving up on that big idea, the fin-vin-gizmo idea that Esperanto would be universally adopted by everyone as a second language.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们基本上放弃了那个大想法，即“最终胜利”的想法，认为世界语会被所有人普遍采纳为第二语言。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And at the time, in 1980, the language had been around for nearly a century.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，1980年，这门语言已经存在了近一个世纪。

sentences.en: That final victory hadn't happened yet.
sentences.zh: 那个“最终胜利”还没有实现。

sentences.en: So, this group of young folks proposed that the language be viewed more as a community-building tool,
sentences.zh: 于是，这群年轻人提议将这门语言更多地视为一种社区建设工具，

sentences.en: and that Esperanto should consider themselves, quote, as belonging to a self-chosen diasporic linguistic minority.
sentences.zh: 并认为世界语者应该将自己视为“属于一个自选的离散语言少数群体”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, in essence, they're allowing for and kind of accepting the idea that Esperanto would be a subculture.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，他们允许并接受了世界语将成为一种亚文化的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, it didn't have to be universally adopted in order to have value.
sentences.zh: 它不必被普遍采纳也能拥有价值。

sentences.en: You know, I love that there's, you know, like, there's this formal acknowledgement that the language has some limitations,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢这种正式承认这门语言有一些局限性的做法，

sentences.en: but there's still a desire to keep it anyway and to have it to be a thing that people share.
sentences.zh: 但人们仍然渴望保留它，并让它成为人们共享的东西。

sentences.en: But I can't imagine, you know, the final victory folks enjoyed this capitulation at all.
sentences.zh: 但我无法想象那些坚持“最终胜利”的人会喜欢这种妥协。

sentences.en: No, they did not.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不喜欢。

sentences.en: The fin-vin-gizmo folks did not like this.
sentences.zh: “最终胜利”派的人不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But, you know, based on what I saw at the Congress last year, the subculture school of thought really seems to have sort of won out.
sentences.zh: 但是，根据我去年在大会上看到的，亚文化流派似乎真的胜出了。

sentences.en: But what about this old Esperantist thought, you know, the goal of using this language explicitly to promote world peace?
sentences.zh: 但那种老派的世界语思想呢，就是明确利用这门语言来促进世界和平的目标？

sentences.en: Like, I can't imagine the spirit of that is totally gone.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象那种精神已经完全消失了。

sentences.en: No, it's not totally gone.
sentences.zh: 不，它并没有完全消失。

sentences.en: I had some really interesting conversations with very politically dedicated Esperantists,
sentences.zh: 我和一些非常有政治奉献精神的世界语者进行了非常有趣的交谈，

sentences.en: and that peacenik school of thought has lived on in some unlikely places.
sentences.zh: 那种和平主义流派在一些意想不到的地方延续了下来。

sentences.en: As an example, I spoke with a man named Espoir Nagoma-Kassati,
sentences.zh: 例如，我采访了一位名叫埃斯波尔·纳戈马-卡萨蒂的男士，

sentences.en: and he's from the DRC, the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
sentences.zh: 他来自刚果民主共和国（DRC）。

sentences.en: And the DRC is one of the most linguistically diverse nations in the world.
sentences.zh: 刚果民主共和国是世界上语言最多样化的国家之一。

sentences.en: It has more than 200 languages, and it has also been struggling with a brutal conflict.
sentences.zh: 它有200多种语言，也一直在与残酷的冲突作斗争。

sentences.en: And Espoir is part of a contingent trying to advance a pacifist movement
sentences.zh: 埃斯波尔是一个致力于推进和平主义运动的代表团成员，

sentences.en: by bringing people together under one shared language.
sentences.zh: 通过将人们聚集在一种共同的语言下。

sentences.en: Did you get that, Roman?
sentences.zh: 你听懂了吗，罗曼？

sentences.en: Like a little.
sentences.zh: 听懂了一点。

sentences.en: Like, he's saying that many Africans speak Esperanto,
sentences.zh: 他是说很多非洲人说世界语，

sentences.en: a very diverse group of people speak it, something like that.
sentences.zh: 一个非常多样化的群体在说它，类似这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's basically saying that many young Africans in many different countries speak Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 是的，他基本上是说许多不同国家的年轻非洲人在说世界语。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he says that he and his colleagues feel the language is good for Africa
sentences.zh: 他说他和他的同事们觉得这门语言对非洲有好处，

sentences.en: because it's not a colonial language.
sentences.zh: 因为它不是一种殖民语言。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an excellent point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个极好的观点。

sentences.en: Like, they're gathering people from all over the world in this Congress and these big ideas,
sentences.zh: 他们在这个大会上聚集了来自世界各地的人，讨论这些宏大的想法，

sentences.en: and they're all speaking the same language, and for once, it is not English.
sentences.zh: 他们都在说同一种语言，而且难得的是，那不是英语。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: It's a huge accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的成就。

sentences.en: And I think these days, Esperantists, broadly speaking,
sentences.zh: 我认为如今的世界语者，广义上来说，

sentences.en: sort of recognize the utility of having the more politically devout side of the movement
sentences.zh: 认识到了让运动中更具政治虔诚的一面

sentences.en: exist alongside the subculturists.
sentences.zh: 与亚文化派并存的效用。

sentences.en: So at the convention, I spoke with a scholar and a prominent Esperantist named Humphrey Tonkin.
sentences.zh: 所以在大会上，我采访了一位学者和杰出的世界语者，名叫汉弗莱·通金。

sentences.en: He was 85 years old at the time.
sentences.zh: 他当时85岁。

sentences.en: He's a very, very accomplished guy.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常有成就的人。

sentences.en: He was the president of a college.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一所大学的校长。

sentences.en: He's a scholar of literature.
sentences.zh: 他是一位文学学者。

sentences.en: In the Esperanto world, he's definitely a get.
sentences.zh: 在世界语界，他绝对是个大人物。

sentences.en: And he put it this way, which I really liked.
sentences.zh: 他这样表述，我很喜欢。

sentences.en: If you are into the English-speaking peace movement, what are you doing there?
sentences.zh: 如果你参与的是英语世界的和平运动，你在那里做什么？

sentences.en: Peace.
sentences.zh: 和平。

sentences.en: So you talk about peace.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈论和平。

sentences.en: You talk about it really seriously.
sentences.zh: 你谈起这个来真的很严肃。

sentences.en: And you, in fact, probably talk about it so seriously that you bore the hell out of people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你可能谈得太严肃了，以至于让人感到厌烦。

sentences.en: It's not like that in the Esperanto movement because we have a whole culture that we can fall back on.
sentences.zh: 但在世界语运动中并非如此，因为我们有深厚的文化底蕴作为后盾。

sentences.en: So most people I spoke with had no delusions about the language's potential.
sentences.zh: 所以我交谈过的大多数人对这门语言的潜力都没有抱有幻想。

sentences.en: They knew that unlocking world peace is a goal that's poignantly out of their hands.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，开启世界和平是一个他们无能为力的宏大目标，这令人心酸。

sentences.en: But what the Esperantists did show me is that even amid our global turmoil,
sentences.zh: 但世界语者们向我展示的是，即使在我们全球动荡不安的环境中，

sentences.en: they still found it worthwhile to get together to try to enact the ideals of peace and understanding,
sentences.zh: 他们仍然觉得聚在一起努力践行和平与理解的理想是有意义的，

sentences.en: even if only on a small scale and even if only among one another.
sentences.zh: 哪怕只是小范围的，哪怕只是在他们彼此之间。

sentences.en: Yeah, like the movement might not bring the peace that Zemenhoff dreamed of,
sentences.zh: 是的，也许这场运动无法带来柴门霍夫所梦想的那种和平，

sentences.en: but it might bring some measure of peace and understanding to the people who speak it.
sentences.zh: 但它或许能为使用这门语言的人们带来一定程度的和平与理解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And look, it's easy to think of that as an overly optimistic and simplistic idea.
sentences.zh: 听着，人们很容易认为这是一种过于乐观且天真的想法。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得这有什么错。

sentences.en: Like sometimes people can fully comprehend one another and still disagree, still even hate each other.
sentences.zh: 就像有时人们可以完全理解对方，但仍然会产生分歧，甚至憎恨彼此。

sentences.en: Language alone isn't going to erase hatred.
sentences.zh: 单靠语言并不能消除仇恨。

sentences.en: But almost everyone I spoke with said that this gathering gives them hope.
sentences.zh: 但我交谈过的几乎每个人都说，这次聚会给了他们希望。

sentences.en: I mean, the idea of hope is baked right into the name of the language.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希望这个概念本身就融入了这门语言的名字里。

sentences.en: The point about hope, though, is that you never achieve your goal.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于希望的一点是，你永远不会真正实现你的目标。

sentences.en: That's not what it's about.
sentences.zh: 那并不是重点所在。

sentences.en: It's about looking at the world in an optimistic way
sentences.zh: 重点是以乐观的方式看待世界，

sentences.en: and working for something that is positive and that will benefit humankind.
sentences.zh: 并为积极且造福人类的事业而努力。

sentences.en: I don't think that among Esperantists there's a great deal of emphasis on the antagonisMs.
sentences.zh: 我不认为世界语者们过分强调对立。

sentences.en: What we look for is what we have in common, which doesn't mean we're always successful.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找的是共同点，但这并不意味着我们总是能成功。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that I don't get infuriated by many of my fellow Esperantists.
sentences.zh: 这也不意味着我不会被许多世界语同伴气得半死。

sentences.en: And we argue in Esperanto, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且我们还会用世界语争论，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it strikes me that this is a group of people that are just absolutely completely devoted
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这群人给我留下了深刻的印象，他们绝对是全心全意地

sentences.en: to trying to learn something from the differences of each other
sentences.zh: 致力于尝试从彼此的差异中学习，

sentences.en: and to try to embrace those differences and find common ground.
sentences.zh: 并试图拥抱这些差异，寻找共同点。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's this sort of shameless love for humanity in the Esperanto world
sentences.zh: 是的，世界语世界里有一种对人类毫无保留的爱，

sentences.en: that really seems to have fallen out of fashion most everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 这种爱在其他大多数地方似乎已经过时了。

sentences.en: And that's not an impulse I'm eager to beat back with obvious critiques,
sentences.zh: 而我并不急于用显而易见的批评去打击这种冲动，

sentences.en: especially critiques that the Esperantists themselves are fully aware of.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些世界语者自己也完全意识到的批评。

sentences.en: Look, I know in 2026, the Esperanto-speaking community is almost uncomfortably earneSt.
sentences.zh: 听着，我知道在2026年，世界语社区显得有些过于一本正经，甚至让人感到不自在。

sentences.en: Some would say it's cringe.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说这很尴尬。

sentences.en: But I think we could all afford to be a little more cringe.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们大家都应该稍微“尴尬”一点也无妨。

sentences.en: So, Roman, there's one more thing I wanted to tell you about from my time in Berno.
sentences.zh: 那么，罗曼，关于我在伯尔尼的那段时光，还有一件事我想告诉你。

sentences.en: And that's that I actually decided to join the daily practices of the Internazia Coruso,
sentences.zh: 那就是我实际上决定参加“国际合唱团”的日常排练，

sentences.en: or International Chorus.
sentences.zh: 也就是国际合唱团。

sentences.en: Did you actually join the Esperanto Choir?
sentences.zh: 你真的加入了世界语合唱团？

sentences.en: There's an Esperanto Choir, and I had to join it.
sentences.zh: 有一个世界语合唱团，我必须加入它。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not a singer-singer, but I've played instruments and sung in bands since I was a teenager,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不是那种专业的歌手，但我从十几岁起就玩乐器并在乐队里唱歌，

sentences.en: so I figured I'd give it a try.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想还是试一试吧。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我爱死它了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, on the final night of the convention,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在大会的最后一晚，

sentences.en: all the attendees went back to the big concert hall where the opening ceremony was held.
sentences.zh: 所有与会者都回到了举行开幕式的大音乐厅。

sentences.en: And the night ended with us, our scrappy little choir,
sentences.zh: 夜晚以我们这个拼凑起来的小合唱团的表演结束，

sentences.en: saying a local Czech folk tune and a Mozart song that was actually translated by Zamenhof himself.
sentences.zh: 我们唱了一首当地的捷克民歌和一首由柴门霍夫亲自翻译的莫扎特歌曲。

sentences.en: But our showstopper, I think, was an Esperanto translation of the Latin hymn Dona nobis pacem,
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们最精彩的表演是拉丁圣歌《赐予我们和平》的世界语译本，

sentences.en: Grant us peace, or in Esperanto, Donu alni patsom.
sentences.zh: 即“赐予我们和平”，用世界语说是“Donu al ni pacon”。

sentences.en: Look, are we in tune?
sentences.zh: 听着，我们合拍吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不完全是。

sentences.en: But are we trying to find harmony together?
sentences.zh: 但我们是否在努力寻找共同的和谐？

sentences.en: Yes, we are.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在努力。

sentences.en: And we're doing so in not one but two constructed languages.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不是用一种，而是用两种人造语言在这样做。

sentences.en: Esperanto, of course, but also musical notation.
sentences.zh: 当然是世界语，还有乐谱。

sentences.en: That's a universal constructed language, too.
sentences.zh: 那也是一种通用的人造语言。

sentences.en: And no one bats an eye at it.
sentences.zh: 而且没人对此感到大惊小怪。

sentences.en: That's a good point.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: I mean, this performance, you know, like maybe a little off-key,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这场表演，你知道，可能有点走调，

sentences.en: but it seems to me, you know, such a fitting end to your convention
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这似乎是你大会的一个非常贴切的结尾，

sentences.en: because, you know, this is what Esperanto is all about, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，这就是世界语的全部意义所在，对吧？

sentences.en: He's trying to come together, even if it's imperfect.
sentences.zh: 它试图让人们走到一起，即使是不完美的。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for this story.
sentences.zh: 那么，非常感谢你分享这个故事。

sentences.en: It's been fun to revisit Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 重温世界语很有趣。

sentences.en: Thanks for talking with me, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你和我交谈，罗曼。

sentences.zh: 再见。
